text.p: Coca-Cola Co on Tuesday unveiled a long-awaited contour-shaped aluminum can, saying the new packaging innovation would be test-marketed in five U.S. markets early next month.

The soft-drink giant said the new cans would be introduced under its flagship Coca-Cola Classic brandname in four Southwestern markets and in Terre Haute, Ind., where the contour bottle first appeared in 1915.
The new packaging is part of a three-year old initiative to promote the contour shape popularized generations ago by the glass Coke bottle.

Coke hopes the contour shape will distinguish its canned products from those of other soft-drink companies. Company marketing executives say the patented shape is universally familiar to consumers and can even be recognized in the dark.
"The proprietary Coca-Cola contour bottle is one of the world's most powerful equities with consumers," Coca-Cola USA President Jack Stahl said in a statement.

"We view the introduction of the contour can as a learning opportunity to assess operational factors before we consider moving toward commercialization of the package. We want to see how the contour can actually works in the marketplace."

Coca-Cola began testing a steel version of the contour can in Germany in 1994 but had to develop new can-shaping capabilities before it could transfer the innovation to the aluminum cans preferred by U.S. consumers.
Three years ago, Coke introduced a 20-ounce contour-shaped plastic bottle for Coca-Cola Classic with much fanfare and followed it up with a dimpled 20-oz. bottle for Sprite.
Coke executives say the innovations introduced the contour-shape to a new generation of young consumers and consequently helped the company expand its share of the U.S. soft-drink market.
The company said the contour-can introductions would be supported by local television, print and outdoor advertising.
